summary:
COMMERCIAL PHOTOREAL PLANT LIBRARIES: LICENCE AND WEB-FIT SWEEP (research only, 2026-10-17)
Nothing was bought, signed up for, installed or edited. The pages were read with WebFetch and the read-only browser pane. Two exceptions: the e-on/Bentley EULA PDF was auto-saved by WebFetch into the session tool-results folder, and its text was extracted to the scratchpad. Licence clauses below are paraphrased with exact section numbers and URLs, because quoting limits allow one short verbatim excerpt (the Fab clause). The binding wording is at the cited URLs.

HEADLINE
No paid library licence allows plant model files to be committed to a public git repo. Every commercial licence read also requires reasonable technical measures to stop end users extracting the models in an interactive or web product. Plain GLBs on a public static path fail that test.

Today the DeckCraft repo (origin github.com/yorkisestevez/goldenmaplelandscaping, checked in the gm-porcelain-geo checkout) tracks 54 GLBs under public/deckcraft/landscape/, written there by scripts/build-plant-library-v2.mjs (OUT=public/deckcraft/landscape). Any paid asset would need:
(a) a separate non-public asset origin, never in git or git history;
(b) an obfuscated or encrypted container that the lazy viewer chunk decodes;
(c) site Terms of Use that forbid extraction;
(d) in several cases, written confirmation from the vendor.

The Fab EULA s.4(c) states the core condition: you "must restrict end users from extracting or otherwise using Content outside of the Project". Maxtree s.2.2(3), CGTrader s.21A.3, Globe Plants (Final Product definition), The Grove clause 2, Maxon s.13.3(c) and Unity's Asset Store guidance carry the same condition. TurboSquid is stricter: three.js-style open formats are banned unless TurboSquid approves in advance.

SECOND BLOCKER: EDITOR AND TOOL CLAUSES
Several licences forbid putting content into world/level-editing or modelling tools that let users make their own projects or export works:
- Fab s.6(b)(iii)
- Maxtree s.3.2(3)
- TurboSquid s.II.7(c) Open Systems
- The Grove clause 2 (the end product must not be a tool to create real-time presentations)
- Unity support guidance on level editors and user-generated content
DeckCraft is a homeowner design tool. A grep of gm-porcelain-geo/src found no 3D exporters (no GLTFExporter, OBJExporter or USDZExporter). DeckCraft exports stills (SceneStillExport.tsx, photoEngine.ts), a flythrough video (FlythroughRecorder.tsx) and PDFs (renderPdf.ts, PermitSetDialog.tsx). That helps, but whether a design tool counts as an editing tool is open. Treat Fab, Maxtree, Unity and SpeedTree as unclear until the vendor confirms in writing. Asking is outreach, so it is an owner action.

BEST COVERAGE AND REALISM (paid)
1. Maxtree: best match to the 26 species. About 17 at species level:
   - sugar maple, red maple, eastern white pine, redbud, blue spruce, Thuja occidentalis, Buxus microphylla, Spiraea japonica, Syringa vulgaris, Echinacea purpurea
   - hosta (several cultivars), Matteuccia, Hemerocallis, Salvia nemorosa, Calamagrostis x acutiflora 'Overdam', Schizachyrium, Panicum virgatum
   About 8 at genus level:
   - Amelanchier lamarckii, Taxus cuspidata/baccata, Cornus spp., Hydrangea macrophylla (for both hydrangeas), Rudbeckia laciniata, Monarda didyma, Nepeta nervosa
   Ninebark: not found.
   The models are archviz-grade (200k–3M polys per variant) and must be heavily rebuilt for the web. Price per species (FBX): Indie $26, Pro $78, Enterprise $156. About $1,950 (Pro) to $3,900 (Enterprise) for 25 species.
2. Megascans on Fab: the most photoreal (photogrammetry), but almost no Ontario species. Boxwood, Bigleaf Hydrangea, Norway Maple, Norway Spruce and ferns. Prices $1.40–$7.05 Personal, about 10x for Professional.
3. SpeedTree: the best LOD, atlas and billboard pipeline. Any species can be authored. The legacy store confirms Sugar Maple, Red Maple, Eastern White Pine and Colorado Blue Spruce in the Library. Pro $899/yr plus Library $999/yr. Distribution is allowed only as embedded in a named Licensed Production.
4. Xfrog: species-level red maple, white pine, blue spruce, T. occidentalis and lilac. Libraries $79–$99. Sold through TurboSquid or CGTrader, whose licences then govern.

ONLY ROUTES THAT ALSO FIT A PUBLIC REPO
- CC0 or CC BY models (see the earlier sources research).
- Bentley PlantFactory (freeware): its EULA s.2.2 lets you share or sell your own models made in it, if they are not derived from PlantCatalog assets or textures.
- Tree[it] (free, low realism).
- CC0 assets on Blendkit (formerly BlenderKit), some behind its paid plan.
- Commissioned models under a contract that assigns copyright or grants a public-repo and web licence.
Bentley PlantCatalog is now free. Bentley's FAQ allows embedding it in games, but its EULA s.6 forbids distributing the Software (which includes PlantCatalog) in part. That is unclear for the web, and no for a public repo. The official PlantCatalog CC BY 4.0 uploads on Sketchfab remain clean.

LICENCE TIER NUANCES
- Fab: Personal-tier eligibility is measured on revenue from the digital content industry (s.2(a)). A landscaping company may qualify for Personal; the owner should confirm.
- Maxtree: tiers use total revenue. Indie up to US$100k, Pro up to US$250k, Enterprise above.
- SpeedTree: Indie under $100k, Pro under $1M, Enterprise over $1M.
- Evermotion: Standard up to $1M, Professional above.

EXCLUDED OR NOT USABLE FOR A PUBLIC WEB APP
- Chaos Cosmos: Internal Use only, which now covers the Globe Plants library and partner content from Maxtree and Evermotion.
- Botaniq: its FAQ says the licence covers renders, not redistributing the assets.
- The Grove: DeckCraft is a tool and GLBs are extractable.
- Geo-Scatter biome packs: tied to Geo-Scatter or Biome-Reader.
- TurboSquid: no, without prior written approval.

UNVERIFIED
- Evermotion: licence text blocked by a Cloudflare bot check, which I did not bypass.
- Laubwerk: now Maxon Capsules inside Cinema 4D. Maxon One $1,799/yr; s.13.3 allows third-party access only under a contract binding them not to extract.

WEB FIT, ALL PAID ROUTES
Phone budgets are LOD1 for balanced and LOD2 for constrained; stills need LOD0 for 273 plants. Every offline library (Maxtree HP, Xfrog, Globe, Evermotion, Botaniq) needs a build-time rebuild:
- decimate to about 15–25k triangles for trees and 2–8k for perennials at LOD0
- bake leaf and needle atlases at 1–2k, convert to KTX2
- generate LOD1 and an LOD2 billboard (Xfrog includes 800x800 alpha billboards)
Plan about 0.5–1 artist-day per species. Megascans (fbx and gltf) and SpeedTree games exports (LOD, atlas, billboard) are closest to ready. In all cases realism at LOD1/LOD2 will come mostly from our own baking, not the vendor's hero mesh.

PRICE NOTE
Fab prices were displayed without a currency label. They match CAD conversions of US$0.99/2.99/3.99/4.99 ($1.40/4.22/5.64/7.05), so confirm at checkout.

SEARCH BUDGET
The shared WebSearch budget ran out near the end. CGTrader and TurboSquid species-by-species searches and Megascans LOD and polycount details were not finished. Maxtree site searches read only the first page of results for Cornus, Hydrangea, Calamagrostis and Syringa.

RECOMMENDED DECISION PATH
1. Owner decides whether paid plant assets may live outside the public repo, on a private origin with obfuscated containers and Terms of Use. If not, only commissioned work-for-hire, PlantFactory, CC0 or CC BY routes remain.
2. If yes, owner asks Maxtree (coverage) and Unity/SpeedTree (pipeline) in writing whether DeckCraft's use is allowed. Quote the editor/tool clause and the extraction measures.
3. Buy a one-species pilot (for example Maxtree V122_Thuja_occidentalis_01, FBX Indie $26 or Pro $78). Rebuild it to the phone budgets and compare it against a photo at the Corner, Front and bed close-up cameras before buying more.
4. Fill the gaps (ninebark, red-osier dogwood, Annabelle, panicle hydrangea, 'Smaragd', 'Karl Foerster') through a custom commission with a web-and-repo licence. The Maxtree Custom Service and Globe Plants custom requests are quote-only.

Every purchase, account, EULA acceptance and vendor email needs explicit owner approval.

routes.name: Maxtree (Plant Models volumes, Low Poly volumes, individual species, Custom Service)
routes.what: A specialist vendor of high-poly archviz plant models (15,000+ models; scanned leaf and bark textures; GrowFX-built). It sells 'Plant Models Vol N' collections (usually 12 species × 6 variants), Low Poly editions of some volumes, single-species packs (6 variants each), a Custom Service and a Scan Library. Blender editions are also sold on Superhive and Gumroad. Main site: https://maxtree.org/
routes.species_coverage:
Checked by maxtree.org site search on 2026-10-17. Some searches read only the first page of results.
SPECIES LEVEL (about 17):
- Acer saccharum: V17, V26, V48, V50, V142
- Acer rubrum: V65
- Pinus strobus: V67, V126
- Cercis canadensis: V2, V55 (×2), V144
- Picea pungens: V63, V157
- Thuja occidentalis: V122 (the species; no 'Smaragd' cultivar)
- Buxus microphylla: V10 (also B. sempervirens V55)
- Spiraea japonica: V66, plus a V66 Low Poly edition
- Syringa vulgaris: V44
- Echinacea purpurea: V34, V145
- Hosta: V8 'Justine' and 'Rainforest Sunrise', V51 'Blue Mouse Ears' (Low Poly edition exists), V55 'Francee', V175 H. plantaginea
- Matteuccia struthiopteris: V82
- Hemerocallis: V28 fulva, V145 hybridus
- Salvia nemorosa: V175
- Calamagrostis x acutiflora: V65 'Overdam' (Low Poly exists) and V109 acutiflora. No 'Karl Foerster'.
- Schizachyrium scoparium: V161
- Panicum virgatum: V49 (×2), plus a V49 Low Poly edition
GENUS LEVEL (about 8):
- Amelanchier lamarckii: V94, V144
- Taxus cuspidata (V110), T. baccata (V85), T. chinensis. Taxus x media is a hybrid of cuspidata and baccata.
- Cornus kousa, florida, mas, controversa and others. No C. sericea on page 1 of 4.
- Hydrangea macrophylla only (V70, page 1 of 2), standing in for both Annabelle and panicle hydrangea.
- Rudbeckia laciniata: V3
- Monarda didyma: V170
- Nepeta nervosa: V106
NOT FOUND: Physocarpus opulifolius (ninebark).
routes.realism:
High. These are archviz hero models with scanned textures, among the most photoreal plant libraries for close-ups. That realism holds only at the source polycount. Decimating to web budgets is where the look is won or lost, and Maxtree's own Low Poly page says low-poly models are not suitable for games.
Examples:
- https://maxtree.org/3d-plant-models/v122_thuja_occidentalis_01/
- https://maxtree.org/3d-plant-models/plant-models-vol-122/
- https://maxtree.org/3d-plant-models/plant-models-vol-49-low-poly/
routes.licence:
MAXTREE EULA, last update 2026-03-05: https://maxtree.org/eula/ (paraphrased; section numbers exact)
- s.1.2 tiers: Free; Indie (total revenue up to US$100k in the last 12 months, single entity); Pro (up to US$250k, single entity); Enterprise (above US$250k; partners only for co-production under written deletion terms); Custom.
- s.2.1(1): non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to privately use, copy, display, perform and modify. Games are among the permitted fields.
- s.2.2(1): Distribute includes making Project functionality available online.
- s.2.2(2): rendered linear media may be distributed freely only as irreversible final pixel output.
- s.2.2(3): a Project that includes the content as a dependency may go to end users if (1) they get it only in object/target code with no source files, and (2) you take reasonable technical or administrative measures, for example encryption and access controls, to prevent extraction or use outside the Project.
- s.2.3: no standalone distribution to third parties.
- s.3.2(1): no reverse engineering or cracking.
- s.3.2(2): no independent sale; the content must be a component of a value-adding Project.
- s.3.2(3): you may not let third parties incorporate the content into their own products or projects. Level editors, templates and modelling tools that let users export works are the example.
- s.3.2(4): after modification, no channel for third parties to export, extract, download or use the content independently.
- s.3.2(5): derivatives stay with the licensee's internal team; no re-licensing; no external resource library.
TERMS & CONDITIONS: https://maxtree.org/terms-and-conditions/
- s.5.1: no using Maxtree assets to build competing products.
- s.5.2: limited, revocable, non-sublicensable licence.
routes.cost:
Prices read from the product variation data on maxtree.org, USD.
SINGLE SPECIES (6 variants), e.g. V122_Thuja_occidentalis_01:
- FBX: Indie $26 / Pro $78 / Enterprise $156
- Mesh: $36 / $109 / $218
- GrowFX+Mesh: $61 / $184 / $368
HIGH-POLY COLLECTION, e.g. Vol 122:
- FBX: $125 / $375 / $750
- Mesh: $175 / $525 / $1,050
- GrowFX: $295 / $885 / $1,770
LOW-POLY COLLECTION, e.g. Vol 49 LP:
- FBX: $105 / $315 / $630
- Mesh: $155 / $465 / $930
OTHER:
- Superhive Blender editions: $175 per volume
- Samples Vol 1: $5; Vol 60 is a free trial
ESTIMATE: about 25 species bought singly in FBX costs about $650 (Indie), $1,950 (Pro) or $3,900 (Enterprise).
Custom Service for the missing species is quote-only.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Confirm the revenue tier: Indie up to $100k, Pro up to $250k, Enterprise above.
2. Approve the spend and create a Maxtree account; accept the EULA.
3. Approve outreach to Maxtree asking for written confirmation that a public homeowner design tool may serve decimated, encrypted runtime meshes, given s.3.2(3).
4. Approve a non-public asset origin, plus Terms of Use that forbid extraction.
5. Optionally request a Custom Service quote for ninebark, red-osier dogwood, Annabelle, panicle hydrangea, 'Smaragd' and 'Karl Foerster'.
routes.web_fit:
- Formats: FBX (FBX cannot store material parameters, so materials are rebuilt by hand); native .max, .blend (textures not packed), .c4d, .mb, .uasset (UE 5.3.2+), .tmi; .vrscene; GrowFX. No glTF, LODs, atlases or billboards are stated.
- High-poly counts: Thuja occidentalis V122 variants range 204,508–726,764 polys (heights 238–484 cm). The Vol 122 collection ranges about 200,649 to 3,048,040 polys per model.
- Low-poly counts (Vol 49 LP): 360–45,000 per model, e.g. Panicum virgatum 5,146–25,694 and Ligustrum 24,877–45,000.
- Texture resolution is not stated; maps are albedo, gloss, normal, opacity and translucency.
- Path to three.js: import the FBX into Blender. Rebuild or decimate to about 15–25k triangles for a tree LOD0 and 2–8k for perennials. Bake 1–2k leaf and bark atlases and convert to KTX2. Make LOD1 at about 30% and LOD2 as a billboard cloud, then export quantised GLB into an encrypted container.
- Effort: about 0.5–1 artist-day per species. The 273-plant showcase at LOD0 would land around 4–6M triangles; acceptable for desktop stills, not for phones.
routes.risks:
- s.3.2(3) editor clause: DeckCraft lets users make their own designs, though it exports only images, video and PDF.
- Extraction: anything a browser can render can be captured. The licence asks for reasonable measures, not perfect ones.
- The 54 GLBs are currently committed in the public repo. A paid asset leaking into git history would breach s.2.3 and s.3.2(5).
- The revocable-licence wording in Terms s.5.2.
- Misdeclaring the tier.
- Cultivars do not match ('Overdam' instead of 'Karl Foerster'; no 'Smaragd'; Hydrangea macrophylla instead of arborescens or paniculata).
- Site search was only partly read (page 1 of several for some genera).
- Low-poly editions are not game-optimised.

routes.name: Fab: Quixel Megascans 3D plants
routes.what: Epic's Fab marketplace, seller Quixel Megascans: photogrammetry-scanned 3D plants under the Fab Standard License. Since 2025 most Megascans assets are paid per asset; some remain free. Seller page: https://www.fab.com/sellers/Quixel%20Megascans
routes.species_coverage:
Searched the Quixel seller on Fab for hosta, fern, spruce, yew, lilac, daylily and coneflower.
SPECIES LEVEL: none confirmed.
GENUS LEVEL:
- Boxwood: Buxus, species unstated, probably B. sempervirens
- Bigleaf Hydrangea: H. macrophylla, as a stand-in for both hydrangeas
- Norway Maple: Acer, a stand-in for sugar and red maple
- Norway Spruce: Picea, a stand-in for Picea pungens
- Lady Fern, Beech Fern, Bracken and other ferns: a stand-in for the ostrich fern, but not Matteuccia
NOT FOUND: hosta, daylily, coneflower, Rudbeckia, lilac, yew, Thuja, white pine, redbud, serviceberry, dogwood, ninebark, spirea, Nepeta, Salvia, Monarda, and the three grasses. Fuzzy results such as Tundra Grass and Ribbon Grass are not matches.
Megascans is strongest on European flora.
routes.realism:
Best in class: real-world photogrammetry, with translucency, opacity and displacement maps. At close range it reads as a photo, but only for the species it covers.
Examples:
- https://www.fab.com/listings/ae90090d-cafb-4431-a74f-8cded15f93e1 (Boxwood)
- https://www.fab.com/listings/b8220edc-bf7f-4ab4-8618-3ae8209ac433 (Bigleaf Hydrangea)
routes.licence:
FAB END USER LICENSE AGREEMENT (Standard License), last updated October 1, 2024: https://www.fab.com/eula
- s.2(a): Personal tier only if you and your affiliates have no more than US$100,000 gross revenue from commercial activity in the digital content industry in the last 12 months. Advances and funds raised count. Under-paying must be made good on request.
- s.3(a): non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to privately use, reproduce, display, perform and modify.
- s.4(a): Distribute includes making a copy available publicly or making the Project's functionality available on a network, so a website is a Distribution.
- s.4(b): rendered linear media may be distributed freely.
- s.4(c): a Project with Content as an included dependency may go to end users, in object code only. The Project must restrict end users from extracting or using the Content outside it (exact clause quoted in the summary).
- s.5(a): no standalone distribution to third parties, except to collaborators through a private repository, who must delete it afterwards. A public repo is therefore excluded.
- s.6(a): no combining with GPL, LGPL or CC BY-SA content that would relicense it.
- s.6(b)(i): no reverse engineering.
- s.6(b)(ii): the Content must be merely a component, not the primary focus.
- s.6(b)(iii): no letting third parties incorporate Content into their own products or projects. The example given is world- or level-editing tools, templates or modelling tools that allow works to be exported.
- s.16(l): NoAI-tagged content may not be used for AI training. Megascans listings show Allows usage with AI: No.
routes.cost:
Prices are as displayed on fab.com on 2026-10-17. The currency is not labelled; the figures match CAD conversions of US$0.99/2.99/3.99/4.99.
- Boxwood: Personal $7.05 / Professional $70.70. Professional is for entities with more than $100k revenue or funding.
- Many Megascans plants: $1.40–$7.05 Personal; Professional is about 10x.
- Free: Bigleaf Hydrangea, Norway Maple, Common Hazel, Lady Fern.
- Fab EULA s.2(a) measures revenue only from the digital content industry, so Golden Maple may qualify for Personal. This needs owner or legal confirmation.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Create an Epic account; accept the Fab EULA.
2. Confirm the tier.
3. Approve outreach to Epic or Fab support for written confirmation that a homeowner design web app with encrypted runtime meshes is not a world- or level-editing tool under s.6(b)(iii).
4. Approve a non-public asset origin plus Terms of Use.
routes.web_fit:
- Formats: fbx and gltf.
- Size: Boxwood raw zip is 384.21 MB; 1,021 MB in total with its extra file.
- Maps: Basecolor, Normal, Roughness, Gloss, Specular, Translucency, Opacity, AO, Cavity, Bump, Displacement.
- LODs and polycounts are not shown on the listing. Megascans 3D plants usually ship several LODs and variants, but that was not verified here.
- Pipeline: pick variants, cut textures to 1–2k, atlas, convert to KTX2, and make a billboard LOD2.
- This is the closest paid source to real-time-ready, but it covers too few target species.
routes.risks:
- Species mismatch: European species, and homeowners will notice.
- The s.6(b)(iii) editor clause.
- The s.4(c) extraction requirement.
- The s.5(a) public-repo ban; currently 54 GLBs sit in git.
- Revenue-tier back-pay under s.2(a).
- Content Licensors can take content down, so re-downloads are not guaranteed (s.3(b)); keep a private backup.

routes.name: Fab third-party sellers (includes the former Unreal Engine Marketplace and Sketchfab Store 'Standard' listings)
routes.what: Fab is now the store for former Unreal Marketplace products and migrated Sketchfab Store paid and free Standard models. Sketchfab's migration blog says Standard licences map to the Fab Standard licence at the Personal tier, and CC BY listings stay CC BY: https://sketchfab.com/blogs/community/fab-publishing-portal-open-for-sketchfab-migration. Many independent sellers list named North American species.
routes.species_coverage:
Many species-named listings exist; each needs vetting. Examples found by Fab site search:
- Acer saccharum: 14_tree 'Sugar_Maple_a/b/c' (fbx/gltf/glb/obj); ScansLibrary 'Sugar Maple (T45stz)' (a UE scanned material); 'Sugar Maple Tree (Fall) #01–#06'.
- Hosta: 20+ listings, including 'Halcyon', 'Patriot', H. plantaginea, 'Stained Glass', 'White Feather', and 'Foliage - Patriot Hosta - PBR Game Ready'.
- Thuja: 'Eastern Arborvitae', 'Fire Chief', 'Tiny Tim', 'Mr. Bowling Ball', 'Hetz Midget', 'Realistic Arborvitae (Thuja) Tree'.
- UE-only packs, e.g. LA Archviz 'Realistic Garden Plants for Archviz – Pack 01' (species not listed).
The other species were not searched individually (search budget). Expect broad but uneven coverage.
routes.realism:
Highly variable: from scan-based (ScansLibrary, 4096 px) to mid-quality GLB trees. The 14_tree GLB warns that its glTF/GLB has no opacity maps, so leaves would render as solid cards without rework.
Examples:
- https://www.fab.com/listings/377ff5a0-ad78-44e3-ac42-d4e64f172cea
- https://www.fab.com/listings/db317aca-ee1d-433c-b330-f157eebb16f7
- https://www.fab.com/listings/2315d99b-ec8c-41c7-b58d-8f237e13fb9a
routes.licence:
Standard License listings use the Fab EULA (https://www.fab.com/eula); see the Megascans route for s.2(a), s.4(c), s.5(a) and s.6(b)(iii).
CC BY listings fall under Fab EULA s.2(c) and (d)(iii): the open licence governs. Those are fine for a public repo with attribution.
Some listings say Allows usage with AI: Yes (e.g. 14_tree); that does not change the distribution rules.
routes.cost:
Displayed prices (currency unlabelled):
- 14_tree Sugar_Maple_c: $22.61–$29.68 (Personal–Professional)
- ScansLibrary Sugar Maple scan: $4.22–$21.20
- LA Archviz Pack 01: $14.12–$42.41
- Others vary.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve each purchase on an Epic account.
2. Approve outreach to each seller about provenance, i.e. whether the model was made with SpeedTree or The Grove, whose output may not be resold.
3. The same Fab confirmation as the Megascans route.
routes.web_fit:
- Some listings ship GLB directly; the 14_tree maple zip is 5.66 MB.
- Many are UE-only (.uasset with Nanite, Lumen and path tracing) and would need export from Unreal.
- Expect to redo alpha, atlases and LODs.
routes.risks:
- Seller provenance: resold SpeedTree, Grove or Xfrog output.
- The same Fab extraction, editor-tool and public-repo constraints.
- Inconsistent quality.
- AI-generated content flags.

routes.name: SpeedTree (Unity): Modeler subscriptions and the SpeedTree Library
routes.what: An industry-standard procedural vegetation modeler with game exports (LODs, atlases, billboards, wind), plus a Library of hundreds of ready-made trees and plants. Sold only through Unity since 2026; store.speedtree.com now redirects to https://unity.com/products/speedtree. Individual library asset purchases were discontinued from May 2026; the Library is now an annual subscription.
routes.species_coverage:
LIBRARY: legacy store listings, seen in search snippets, confirm:
- Sugar Maple ('Field' and 'Forest')
- Red Maple (single SPM at about 741,070 triangles medium resolution; a 4-model species pack)
- Eastern White Pine (4-model species pack)
- Colorado Blue Spruce (Hero Tree Package)
The other 22 species could not be verified: the catalogue is behind the purchase login, so ask SpeedTree support for a list.
MODELER: any of the 26, including cultivars, can be authored with our own CC0 photo-based leaf and bark textures; output counts as Created Assets.
routes.realism:
High: used in AAA games and feature film. With good leaf and bark textures, trees hold up at close range. Shrubs and perennials depend on the artist.
Example: https://unity.com/products/speedtree
routes.licence:
UNITY PROFESSIONAL ARTISTRY ADDITIONAL TERMS (covers SpeedTree), last updated September 10, 2026: https://unity.com/legal/professional-artistry-additional-terms
- s.3.2.2: a Created Asset is any mesh, procedural model file or texture you make with the software.
- s.3.2.4: a Library Asset is one supplied in a Speedtree Asset Library.
- s.3.2.5: a Licensed Production is the specific production identified by name in the Order Form, including an interactive or real-time application.
- s.2.1.3 (Created Assets): perpetual, royalty-free, non-sublicensable licence, solely to create and distribute Licensed Productions.
- s.2.1.3.1: incorporate only together with substantial original content, used only as an embedded component that is not a substantial portion of the production.
- s.2.1.3.2: reproduce, display, transmit and distribute only as incorporated and embedded in the Licensed Production.
- s.2.1.2: the same terms for Library Assets.
- s.2.4: no exporting from Learning or Evaluation editions.
SPEEDTREE FAQ (https://unity.com/products/speedtree): the SpeedTree Terms of Service do not allow resale or redistribution of trees.
UNITY SUPPORT: https://support.unity.com/hc/en-us/articles/15723346606484 says Created and Library Assets may be distributed only in Licensed Productions, and selling them is prohibited.
routes.cost:
From the plans on https://unity.com/products/speedtree:
- Indie: US$19/month (funding or revenue under $100k)
- Pro: US$899/year (under $1M)
- Library add-on: US$999/year subscription, Games or Cinema (under $1M), not included in any plan
- Enterprise: custom price via sales@speedtree.com (over $1M); includes the Runtime SDK and library options
- Pro + Library = US$1,898 per year
- A 30-day trial exists, but exports have random polygons removed
routes.owner_actions:
1. Confirm the revenue band.
2. Approve the subscription and a Unity ID; accept the Terms.
3. Approve outreach to licensing@speedtree.com or sales@speedtree.com asking (a) how to name DeckCraft as the Licensed Production on a self-serve subscription, (b) whether browser-delivered, encrypted runtime meshes count as embedded distribution, and (c) whether a plant library inside a yard designer is a 'substantial portion'.
4. Ask what happens to Library assets after the subscription lapses.
5. Approve a non-public asset origin.
routes.web_fit:
- Games exports: OBJ, FBX, USD, ST/STSDK, CGF, XML, with game-ready texture atlases, LODs and billboards. Wind is exported. The Library ships 8K PBR textures.
- No glTF export is listed; convert FBX to glTF/KTX2 at build time.
- The best tooling for hitting the LOD0/LOD1/LOD2 phone budgets and for 273-plant LOD0 stills: author directly at, for example, 20k/6k/billboard.
- The Modeler needs internet access for Indie and Pro.
routes.risks:
- The Licensed Production must be named.
- The 'substantial portion' and embedded-only conditions.
- The FAQ's blanket no-redistribution line.
- Revenue caps.
- Library contents are unverified for 22 species.
- Continuity of the Unity-owned product.
- A public repo is clearly excluded.

routes.name: Bentley / e-on PlantCatalog (now freeware) and its official CC BY Sketchfab uploads
routes.what: e-on's PlantCatalog, a procedural plant library with HD, LD and RT (real-time) variants, built with PlantFactory. Bentley discontinued development and made VUE, PlantFactory and PlantCatalog free perpetual downloads: https://www.bentley.com/software/e-on-software-free-downloads/. The official PlantCatalog Sketchfab account has 2,309 models under CC BY 4.0.
routes.species_coverage:
VERIFIED (earlier Sketchfab research):
- Picea pungens: 'Koster' and 'Glauca Globosa', CC BY 4.0, species level
- Dryopteris filix-mas: genus stand-in for the ostrich fern
- Plus Quercus rubra, Norway, Engelmann and black spruce, which are not targets
FULL FREE COLLECTION: species list not retrieved. The 2020 launch had 60 species, with 10–20 added per quarterly update; a 'North American Pine Forest' update added 19 species, which may include Pinus strobus (unverified). The owner or an agent can browse the free archives.
routes.realism:
High, archviz grade: procedural PlantFactory plants with scanned textures and season and age presets.
Example: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/8c114e3b958e48298a97cc5da6efb1f0 (Colorado Blue Spruce 'Koster', 44,675 faces)
routes.licence:
e-on SOFTWARE EULA (Bentley Systems International), PDF linked from the download page: https://www.bentley.com/link/efb8b569396041b28dec5a40b8a000c4.aspx
- s.1.5: Software means VUE, PlantFactory and PlantCatalog, provided for free download.
- s.2.1: free, non-exclusive right to install and use.
- s.2.2: no selling of any assets wholly or partly derived from PlantCatalog assets, materials or texture maps.
- s.5: no rental or commercial hosting of the Software.
- s.6: any reproduction, transfer or distribution of the Software, in part or in full, without Bentley's written permission is forbidden.
- s.7: no reverse engineering.
BENTLEY DOWNLOAD-PAGE FAQ (same URL as above): models may be used commercially, for example embedded in games, shared with clients or embedded in project files. Derived models may not be resold on marketplaces. All plants are copyrighted by Bentley.
CC BY 4.0 Sketchfab uploads: attribution and indication of changes; redistribution is allowed.
routes.cost: Free. The old subscription was US$249.95/year for Standard (with exporter) and US$99/year for Creator.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve downloading the VUE and PlantFactory perpetual builds and each plant archive. Each archive is a self-extracting installer, i.e. a Windows executable.
2. Accept the EULA.
3. Optionally approve outreach to Bentley for written confirmation of web-app embedding. EULA s.6 conflicts with the FAQ.
No spend.
routes.web_fit:
- Historic HD/LD/RT variants; RT was meant for game engines.
- The standalone PlantCatalog Exporter is no longer available; PlantFactory now provides export (FBX/OBJ/Alembic and others).
- The CC BY Sketchfab GLBs are 23–70 MB, 37k–81k faces and 13–30 textures each, so they need decimation and atlasing.
routes.risks:
- The full free collection may not cover the target species.
- The EULA s.6 'in part' wording versus the FAQ's games permission.
- No support or updates.
- Running vendor installers is an owner action.
- Only the CC BY uploads are safe for a public repo.

routes.name: Bentley / e-on PlantFactory (freeware): build our own species
routes.what: PlantFactory is the procedural plant modeler PlantCatalog was built with, now free. A route to photoreal species we own, using our own CC0 or purchased textures.
routes.species_coverage: Any of the 26, including the cultivars 'Smaragd', 'Annabelle' and 'Karl Foerster'. Every model has to be authored by us or by a contractor.
routes.realism: Capable of PlantCatalog-level realism, but only with skilled authoring and good leaf, bark and flower textures. Realistically it is a multi-week effort for 26 species. Download page: https://www.bentley.com/software/e-on-software-free-downloads/
routes.licence: e-on Software EULA s.2.2 (PDF above): sharing or selling User-Made Assets created in VUE or PlantFactory, as generic 3D files or images, is permitted, provided they are not derived from PlantCatalog assets, materials or textures. Section 1.9 defines User Made Assets as model files, textures and meshes created with the Software.
routes.cost: Free software; artist time is the cost.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve installing the Bentley free builds (a Windows installer).
2. Approve the artist time, or a contractor.
routes.web_fit: Export to generic mesh formats, then convert to glTF/KTX2 at build time. LODs and atlases are authored by us.
routes.risks:
- Discontinued software.
- A learning curve.
- PlantCatalog textures or metanodes must not leak into our models.
- Photo-level realism is not guaranteed and depends on the textures.

routes.name: Xfrog (XfrogPlants libraries)
routes.what: Procedurally modelled plants with scanned leaves, bark and flowers: 7,000+ plants in 31 libraries of 20 species × 3 ages (60 models each). Store: https://www.xfrog.net/shop. The product pages say to buy on TurboSquid or CGTrader. Earlier Xfrog uploads on Sketchfab are CC BY-NC-ND, so not usable.
routes.species_coverage:
About 10 of the 31 libraries were read.
LIBRARY CONTENTS:
- USA East: Acer rubrum, Pinus strobus, Thuja occidentalis
- USA Conifers: Picea pungens var. glauca, Pinus strobus
- Shrubs: Syringa vulgaris; Cornus mas and sanguinea
- Landscaping: Buxus sempervirens (also hedges and golden-leaved), Taxus baccata, Thuja plicata and orientalis
- Blossoming: Cercis siliquastrum, Cornus kousa
- Flowers 3: Hydrangea sp.
- HD Flowers 3: Buxus, Hydrangea macrophylla
SPECIES LEVEL (5): red maple, eastern white pine, Colorado blue spruce, Thuja occidentalis (not 'Smaragd'), common lilac.
GENUS LEVEL: boxwood, yew, redbud, dogwood, both hydrangeas, sugar maple (via Acer platanoides or campestre).
NOT FOUND in the libraries read: Amelanchier, Physocarpus, Spiraea, and every perennial and grass target.
routes.realism:
Good at mid-distance. It is an older generation than scans or Maxtree, so it is less convincing in close-up.
Example: https://www.xfrog.net/product-page/library-usa-east
routes.licence: No Xfrog EULA was found: xfrog.net/license returns 404. The product pages send buyers to TurboSquid or CGTrader, so the licence is the marketplace's (see those routes). Forum reports (unverified) say ready-made Xfrog plants may not be passed to others.
routes.cost:
- Library: US$99 regular, $79 sale
- Regional collections: $199
- XFROG WORLD: $599
- 3,000-plant bundle: $499; Volume 1 or 2: $299
- Free single samples, e.g. Calocedrus decurrens, Acer campestre
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve purchase on CGTrader (more permissive text) rather than TurboSquid.
2. Approve outreach to Xfrog support to confirm which licence applies.
routes.web_fit:
- Formats: FBX, OBJ, 3DS, MAX (Arnold/V-Ray/Redshift/Corona/Forest Pack), C4D, Maya, LightWave, Modo, MicroStation, Maxwell, VUE, Terragen, XFR.
- Each library includes 60 billboards and 60 perspective renders at 800×800 with alpha, which are directly useful as LOD2 impostors.
- Polycounts and LODs are not stated, so expect offline density and decimation.
routes.risks:
- Licence depends on the marketplace.
- Dated look.
- Weak perennial and grass coverage.
- TurboSquid's licence bans three.js delivery without pre-approval.

routes.name: Globe Plants (library moved to Chaos Cosmos; custom-request service still open)
routes.what: Australian archviz and VR plant studio. All existing library assets have moved to Chaos Cosmos, and the online store is closed. The Custom Request service still makes new species to order. https://globeplants.com/
routes.species_coverage:
LIBRARY (now in Cosmos):
- Bundle 43 Canadian Plants: 15 species, 91 models; species not listed on cgtricks.com
- Bundle 52 North American Trees: 86 models
CUSTOM REQUESTS: could cover all 26, including the cultivars, from botanical names plus reference photos.
routes.realism: High: archviz/VR grade with season and age variants and GrowFX-editable foliage. https://globeplants.com/
routes.licence:
GLOBE PLANTS EULA: https://globeplants.com/pages/end-user-license-agreement-eula
- s.2: non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual, royalty-free right to download, modify and distribute Final Products, once paid.
- s.3: permitted uses include archviz, VFX, games, VR/AR/MR, product visualisation and web or print marketing. Final Products include real-time scenes and interactive applications.
- Final Product definition: the assets must not be extractable by an end user in any editable form.
- s.4: no resale, sublicensing, sharing, giving away or other redistribution of the Licensed Assets or derivatives in any form; no inclusion in open-source, stock or marketplace offerings.
- s.5: all rights in the Licensed Assets stay with Globe Plants. There is no work-for-hire clause.
routes.cost: Custom models are quoted individually. Turnaround is about 5–7 business days for fewer than 5 species; no volume discounts. The library itself now comes only through a Chaos subscription (see Chaos Cosmos).
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve outreach for a quote, which is a form submission.
2. Negotiate the deliverables: glTF or FBX with real-time LODs at our budgets.
3. Ideally negotiate a written licence term allowing encrypted web delivery, or a copyright assignment.
4. Approve the spend.
routes.web_fit: Delivered in 3ds Max, GrowFX, FBX, SketchUp, C4D, Blender, Twinmotion, Rhino, Redshift or UE5. Polycounts are not stated; real-time LODs must be specified in the commission.
routes.risks:
- The EULA keeps the IP with Globe and bans redistribution, so the files must never enter the public repo.
- 'Not extractable in any editable form' is a high bar for WebGL, so encryption is needed.
- Quote-only pricing.
- Turnaround for 26 species is uncertain.

routes.name: Chaos Cosmos (V-Ray, Corona, Enscape asset library)

From https://www.thegrove3d.com/buy:

- Twigs: €9.69 each, or €6.79 each when buying 10 or more

routes.name: CGTrader Royalty Free License (marketplace)

routes.species_coverage: Broad but per listing; Xfrog libraries are sold here (see the Xfrog route). Species-by-species searches were not completed because the search budget ran out. A third-party hosta was seen at about US$19 (MAX/FBX).

routes.licence:
CGTRADER TERMS s.21A (Royalty Free License): https://www.cgtrader.com/pages/terms-and-conditions
- s.21A.1: products may not be sold, given or assigned to others in the form downloaded from the site.
- s.21A.2: licence limited to Incorporated Product. Approved uses include: games (product inside a proprietary format); virtual worlds, metaverses, applications or platforms, provided users cannot download the product in its downloaded form and it is not re-packaged as goods; and a creative tool's bundled end-user asset library that lets users freely use the product in their own creative projects, limited to Incorporated Product.
- s.21A.3: in software products you must take all commercially reasonable measures to stop end users gaining access, e.g. proprietary format, protected database or resource file, or encrypting the data.

routes.name: TurboSquid 3D Model License (Standard; Enterprise/Agency upgrades)

- Maxtree volumes as Blender editions (see Maxtree), e.g. Vol 21 at $175 (15 species, 131 models).
- 'Thuja Smaragd Collection vol 138-Blender' (creator jimi_boyyy / seller '3D Green Box'): Thuja occidentalis 'Smaragd', species and cultivar level. https://superhivemarket.com/products/thuja-smaragd-collection-vol-138-blender
routes.realism: Maxtree volumes are high. The Smaragd collection is unknown quality; the listing is textured and normal-mapped.
routes.licence: SUPERHIVE STANDARD ROYALTY-FREE (https://support.superhivemarket.com/article/226-understanding-product-license-types): commercial use and modification allowed; redistribution only with the creator's permission; no attribution needed. The article does not address games or extraction.
routes.cost:
- Smaragd collection: US$7.00
- Maxtree Blender volumes: US$175 each
routes.owner_actions: Approve the purchase and outreach to the creator for written web-runtime permission.
routes.web_fit: Smaragd collection: FBX and OBJ, 346,470 polys and 472,906 verts in total, Cycles materials. Decimation is needed.
routes.risks:
- Redistribution needs the creator's permission.
- Seller identity is inconsistent on the page.
- Provenance.

routes.name: Blendkit (formerly BlenderKit): paid plan CC0 assets
routes.what: A Blender asset library, renamed Blendkit (blenderkit.com now redirects to blendkit.com). Some CC0 assets need the paid plan. https://www.blendkit.com/plans/pricing/
routes.species_coverage: Thin. Earlier research found CC0 paid assets such as Norway Spruce and Boxwood Hedge 2M/4M (genus level); Royalty Free hostas.
routes.realism: Varies by uploader.
routes.licence:
BLENDKIT LICENCES (https://www.blendkit.com/docs/licenses/):
- CC0: rights waived, so redistribution and a public repo are fine.
- Royalty Free: commercial use without attribution, but no resale in the same form, e.g. as a model, an asset pack or a game level on a marketplace.
Earlier research found that the Royalty Free terms allow games only when files cannot easily be extracted.
routes.cost:
- Full: US$9/month (or $90)
- Business: US$29/month per seat (5 or fewer employees, $100k or less revenue)
routes.owner_actions: Approve the subscription and an account; install the add-on.
routes.web_fit: .blend through the add-on; export glTF from Blender.
routes.risks: 'yes' applies only to CC0-licensed items; check each asset's licence field. Coverage is thin.

routes.name: Tree[it] (Evolved Software, free)
routes.what: A free real-time tree generator from 2012 with adjustable LOD, wind data in vertex colours, and FBX/OBJ/DBO/X export. http://www.evolved-software.com/treeit/treeit
routes.species_coverage: Trees only, authored by hand. No presets for the target species are listed.
routes.realism: Low to mid; dated, and not photoreal at close range.
routes.licence: The site FAQ says models made in Tree It can be sold, provided they are your own work. No other licence text was found.
routes.cost: Free.
routes.owner_actions: Approve installing a Windows DirectX 9-era tool, if wanted.
routes.web_fit: FBX (ASCII) and OBJ with adjustable LOD; easy to bring into glTF.
routes.risks: Does not meet the photoreal bar on its own; abandoned-ware risk.

routes.name: Commissioned custom species with a web-and-public-repo licence (work-for-hire)
routes.what: Pay a plant modelling studio or freelancer to build the missing species, or all 26, under a contract that assigns copyright or grants an explicit licence for public repo plus web runtime. Candidates: the Maxtree Custom Service (maxtree.org, CUSTOM SERVICE menu) and Globe Plants Custom Requests (https://globeplants.com/). Their standard EULAs keep the IP, so ownership must be negotiated.
routes.species_coverage: All 26, including the 'Smaragd', 'Annabelle' and 'Karl Foerster' cultivars and Ontario-accurate forms.
routes.realism: As good as the studio. Globe and Maxtree work is archviz grade.
routes.licence: Contract-defined. Without a negotiated term, the vendor EULA applies: Globe EULA s.4 and s.5 (no redistribution, IP stays with Globe) and Maxtree EULA s.2.3 and s.3.2.
routes.cost: Quote only; no published rates. Globe: 5–7 business days for fewer than 5 species, no volume discounts.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve outreach for quotes.
2. Approve the contract terms (copyright assignment or a perpetual licence for public repo and web).
3. Approve the spend.
4. Approve the reference photos supplied.
routes.web_fit: Specify glTF 2.0 deliverables: LOD0 about 15–25k triangles for trees and 2–8k for perennials, LOD1 at about 30%, an LOD2 billboard, 1–2k atlases, KTX2, and botanical-scale dimensions.
routes.risks: Cost and turnaround uncertainty; quality control; the IP clause must be explicit.
